newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan backs tight limit on bank/commerce mix.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan backs tight limit on bank/commerce mix.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Thursday said he backed tight limits on the ability of commercial companies to own banks, and vice versa.
A financial reform bill recently passed by the House Banking Committee would allow banks to derive 15 percent of their revenue from commercial activities, and vice versa, subject to certain limits.

Testifying before a House Commerce subcommittee, Greenspan suggested that the limit be set "significantly" below 15 percent, without specifying a figure. The smaller the figure, the more comfortable he would be, the central bank chief said.
"If we dramatically change the rules now about banking and commerce under circumstances of great uncertainty ... we may well end up doing more harm than good," Greenspan said.
